newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ's Birch warns of investment bubble after easing.
newsitem.headline: NZ's Birch warns of investment bubble after easing.

text.p: New Zealand Finance Minister Bill Birch said on Friday he was concerned that a market-led reduction in interest rates and exchange rates in recent months ought to be balanced to avoid a burst of speculative investment.

"The market-led reduction in interest and exchange rates must be balanced to avoid a burst of speculative investment, in property for example, which may put pressure on the economy," he said in the text of a speech delivered to a business breakfast.
What he called the "rebalancing" of monetary conditions was also positive for long-term growth. "An export-led recovery gives New Zealand a much longer growth cycle," he added.

Average short-term interest rates have fallen to around 8.30 percent from over 10 percent in the latter half of last year, while the kiwi dollar is trading at around 65 U.S. cents compared with 71 in late 1996

The Treasury forecasts a resurgence in economic growth at the end of this year which it seen sustained for the next three years at an average rate of 3.4 percent, although some market economists have produced much less bullish outlooks.
Birch said he believed that exporters were now well-placed, after going through a couple of years when they had maintained export levels mainly through improved efficiency and productivity.

He described as "significant" a survey of business confidence on Thursday that showed export intentions had remained stable during 1997 and a net 23 perent of those surveyed expected to increase exports.
